name: Job Accelerator and Growth Program
provider: Government of Newfoundland and Labrador, Department of Jobs, Growth and Rural Development

summary.quote: The program will promote economic growth and development by providing a payroll rebate on qualifying incremental job creation.

sources.title: Job Accelerator and Growth Program - Jobs, Growth and Rural Development
sources.terms_note: The province owns the copyright and grants the public permission to use the information on its website; third-party graphics, audio and video may not be reproduced.

funding_types.quote: This non-repayable contribution will be provided to the company at a standard rate of 10 per cent of the yearly incremental gross salaries.

cost_share.text: A rebate of 10% of the yearly gross salaries of the new jobs
cost_share.quote: This non-repayable contribution will be provided to the company at a standard rate of 10 per cent of the yearly incremental gross salaries.

criteria.text: The money is for creating new jobs
criteria.quote: providing a payroll rebate on qualifying incremental job creation

criteria.text: Not wholesale or retail (residential and commercial real estate services and lower-growth services such as call centres are also left out)
criteria.quote: Companies that require an industrial benefits agreement with the Province and those in non-strategic sectors, such as residential and commercial real estate services, wholesale or retail, and lower-growth service operations, such as call centers, will not be eligible.

criteria.text: Create at least 20 new jobs over three years
criteria.quote: Creating a minimum of 20 new jobs over a three-year period;

criteria.text: The new jobs have an average salary of $50,000
criteria.quote: Ensuring that the new jobs have an average salary of $50,000; and

criteria.text: A long-term commitment to the province through capital or other investment
criteria.quote: Demonstrating a long-term commitment to the province through capital or other investment.

criteria.text: An established company with solid management, a record of success and a clear path to growth
criteria.quote: The program aims to attract established companies that are ready to commit to the province long term, have solid management, a record of success, and a clear path to growth.

criteria.text: Not a lower-growth service operation or other non-strategic sector
criteria.quote: those in non-strategic sectors, such as residential and commercial real estate services, wholesale or retail, and lower-growth service operations, such as call centers, will not be eligible

criteria.text: Not a company required to sign an industrial benefits agreement with the province (such as energy and mining companies)
criteria.quote: Companies required to enter into industrial benefits agreements with the province, such as energy and mining companies, are ineligible for this program.

criteria.text: The project wouldn't happen without this program
criteria.quote: Eligible projects shall only include those that would not have been undertaken were it not for the funding provided by the JAG Program

contacts.label: Department of Jobs, Growth and Rural Development
contacts.quote: For more information, please contact the department of Jobs, Growth and Rural Development by email at economicdevelopment@gov.nl.ca or phone 1-833-404-2283

research.notes: Intake: 'Applications will be assessed on a rolling basis' describes how applications are assessed, not that they are accepted any time, so intake is unknown (prefer unknown over guessing continuous). Type: the page calls the payroll rebate a 'non-repayable contribution', so non_repayable (not wage_subsidy). cost_share is the 10% standard rate; the page adds 5% for recent graduates or newcomers with priority skills (not in the percent). No maximum amount. Sector: 'wholesale or retail' gives industry not_in 41 and 44-45; 'residential and commercial real estate services' is only part of sector 53 and 'call centers' only part of 56, so those are unclear; 'lower-growth service operations' is too vague to map, so it is a check-this-yourself item as well. The benefits-agreement exclusion ('such as energy and mining companies') is not a sector rule because not every energy or mining company needs one. No location rule: the page invites companies from outside the province. The 20-job, $50,000-salary and commitment conditions are about the project, not today's business, so they are check-this-yourself. The Program Fact Sheet was not read.
